extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, scientists, and learned readers interested in the method of scientific inquiry
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive criteria and methodological precepts for constructing natural history and deriving axioms by induction; guidance for conducting experiments, choosing particulars, and organising inquiry across the sciences. Emphasises empirical evidence over authority and careful restraint in generalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of common and familiar objects into natural history
rubrics_metrics.description: No judgment can be formed of that which is rare or remarkable without a previous regular examination and discovery of the causes of that which is common; therefore the most common objects must be admitted into our history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate causes of familiar, frequent phenomena (gravity, heat, light, hardness, softness, etc.) rather than assuming them as self-evident. Anti-pattern: treating common phenomena as 'already known' and basing inferences about rare cases on unexamined common cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of mean, sordid, or 'filthy' particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: Mean and splendid instances alike are deserving of admission into natural history; mean and sordid instances can yield valuable light and information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not exclude low-status, small, or repulsive particulars from investigation—they may yield important causes (analogy: finest odors produced from putrid matter). Anti-pattern: fastidious exclusion of examples deemed 'beneath' inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek experiments that 'afford light' rather than immediate profit
rubrics_metrics.description: The method looks for experiments that shall afford light rather than profit: knowledge of simple natures, when sufficiently investigated and defined, resembles light and grants access to general mysteries and axioms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize experiments that clarify fundamental natures and enable further discovery, even if they have no immediate material utility. Example: elements of letters have no meaning separately but are necessary to form speech. Anti-pattern: demanding immediate practical payoff as the sole justification for experiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postpone subtile disputes until after axioms are discovered
rubrics_metrics.description: All subtile disputes and discursive efforts are late and preposterous when introduced subsequently to the discovery of axioms; such subtilties were wasted on words rather than nature in scholastic philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive axioms from experiment first, then use subtile analysis to weigh and interpret results. Anti-pattern: indulging in abstruse scholastic distinctions before establishing empirically grounded axioms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject reliance on authority; ground knowledge in facts and experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject every kind of fiction and imposture and trust the evidence of facts rather than deriving authority from ancients or genealogies of prestige.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base conclusions on collected observations and experiments instead of appealing to earlier authorities. Anti-pattern: retrofitting new facts to conform to received systems or seeking legitimacy by tracing ideas to illustrious predecessors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid premature generalization; restrain from generalizing until proper season
rubrics_metrics.description: Bind yourselves to restrain from generalization until the proper season; it is better to know what is necessary than to imagine full possession of truth prematurely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep judgement in suspense until intermediate steps and sufficient inductive evidence permit reliable generalities. Anti-pattern: jumping from a few instances to universal conclusions (flying off to generalities), thereby ruining inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply the inductive method across all sciences (not only natural philosophy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The inductive method likewise comprehends all sciences (logic, ethics, politics); form histories and tables of invention for passions, civil examples, mental operations, as well as for natural phenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare systematic histories and interpretative tables for diverse domains (anger, fear, memory, heat, vegetation) so the method can be applied beyond physical inquiry. Guidance: the method inspects the nature of things and regulates the mind to apply correctly to each subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow traditional methods for teaching and discourse but not as methods of discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: The prevalent system may be suitable for encouraging discussion, adorning discourse, or the practice of common life, but cannot produce very great progress in discovery; the offered system is not easily adapted to vulgar apprehensions except by effects and works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not abolish existing pedagogical or rhetorical uses; rather recognize their limits and reserve the inductive method for genuine discovery. Anti-pattern: insisting the new method replace ordinary teaching uses where inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct a real model of the world by dissecting and anatomizing nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Found a real model of the world in the understanding as it is found to be, not as man's reason has distorted; this requires diligent dissection and anatomizing of the world and destruction of vain apish imitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to discover ideas 'imprinted' by the Creator in matter (true marks) by careful empirical analysis. Truth and utility are identical: effects are valuable as pledges of truth. Anti-pattern: favoring abstracted, arbitrary abstractions over marks grounded in matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value inventions and their transformative societal effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions are among the most distinguished human actions; certain mechanical discoveries (printing, gunpowder, compass) have changed the state of the world and display the immense difference arts make in human life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize work that leads to inventions or methods facilitating further discovery; recognize different kinds/degrees of ambition (private power, national empire, enlargement of mankind's dominion over the universe).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and mitigate possible misuse of arts and sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: Though arts and sciences can be depraved to malevolent or luxurious purposes, this risk exists for all worldly goods; the exercise of regained power over nature should be governed by right reason and true religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge ethical risks but do not forbear discovery; governance and moral framework are necessary to direct applications rightly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach the art of interpretation as a useful, improvable aid
rubrics_metrics.description: The art of interpreting nature is not absolutely necessary nor perfect, but its precepts are most useful and correct; with a proper history and two commitments (lay aside received opinions; restrain from generalization), men may fall into the way of interpretation without the art, though precepts improve readiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided precepts to accelerate and solidify the interpretative process. Two binding commitments recommended: (1) set aside received opinions; (2) delay generalization until warranted. The art can grow with inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize method so that it reduces dependence on individual genius
rubrics_metrics.description: The method levels men's wits and leaves little to individual superiority, achieving results by certain rules and demonstrations rather than by talent alone; the attempt is to be attributed more to fortune and time than to singular wit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design procedural rules and demonstrations that produce reliable results across practitioners. Anti-pattern: treating discovery as primarily the product of exceptional individual talent rather than systematic method.
